title: Tenant Residency Commitment Lexicon and Automated Audit Stitcher
creator: Asha Rangan
description: Problem: Customers need a concise, auditable way to declare how and where their Hosted API data is stored and retained, plus an automated artifact that proves commitments were honored. Current flows are fragmented: console pin UIs, adhoc export scripts, and manual legal bundles. Objective: ship a tenant-facing Residency Commitment Lexicon (compact, machine-readable declarations) and an Automated Audit Stitcher that produces tamper-evident proof bundles on demand or on schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Add a Residency Commitment editor for each tenant endpoint with selectable fields from the Lexicon and free-text rationale.
API: POST /v1/endpoints/:id/residency accepts a ResidencyDeclaration JSON schema and returns a signed commitment_id.
Audit Stitcher: Generate a time-stamped proof bundle (zip) containing request routing traces, region assignments, retention policy snapshots, and KMS-signed metadata for a given date range.
Evidence bundles are stored for 365 days by default and downloadable by tenant owners or legal contacts with audit logging.
End-to-end tests covering commit/uncommit flows, policy drift detection, and bundle generation are in CI with >90% coverage for the critical paths.
decisions: Use a compact Residency Lexicon (YAML/JSON) with enumerations for residency_level (local, regional, multi-region) and retention_profile (ephemeral, short, standard, long), instead of free-form text fields to enable deterministic matching.
Proof bundles will use signed manifests (HMAC + KMS-wrapped key) rather than full blockchain-style notarization to balance operational complexity with legal acceptability.
Expose both on-demand and scheduled bundle generation; scheduled bundles default to monthly for trial tenants and weekly for enterprise tenants.
tradeoffs: Enumerated lexicon reduces expressiveness for edge compliance cases but greatly simplifies automation and matching logic.
Storing complete routing traces for audit increases storage cost; we mitigate by snapshotting only metadata and prefix/KV cache hashes rather than full payloads.
Signing proof bundles with KMS is simpler than distributed notarization but centralizes trust in our key control plane; compensating control is strict key rotation and HSM-backed keys.
tasks: Define residency lexicon v1 and publish JSON schema
API: Add POST/GET residency endpoints and signed-commitment workflow
Runtime: Emit region assignment traces to audit stream
Audit Stitcher: Compose bundle generator service and storage lifecycle
Legal: Validate proof bundle contents for contractual acceptance
E2E tests and performance validation under high request rates
comments: 2025-02-11 - Asha Rangan: Initial ticket created after legal workshop. Goal is to unify UI + API + audit artifact generation to reduce manual evidence pulls for compliance reviews.
2025-02-14 - Omar Patel: Met with runtime team. ENG-12189 scoped to add region assignment headers and a lightweight trace event. Will rely on existing audit-log pipeline for ingestion.
2025-02-18 - Priya Menon (Legal): Reviewed draft lexicon; requested 'data_subclass' field to capture categories bound by local law (e.g., PII-health). Added to v1 schema as optional enum.
2025-02-21 - Engineering review: Chose KMS-signed manifest approach. Marcelo suggested adding SHA256 hashes of key KV caches instead of raw payloads to reduce exposure. Accepted.

2025-02-25 - Omar Patel: Backend PR opened for API routes (see related_prs). Console mockups handed to DES-5601 for interactive polishing. Scheduling weekly stitcher for enterprise tenants behind feature flag.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Enable feature for Redwood internal orgs and run synthetic audits for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (beta): Opt-in for select enterprise customers; collect legal feedback and iterate
Phase 3 (GA): Turn on for all tenants with default scheduled monthly bundles and tenant-level controls
evidence_format: bundle.zip contains: manifest.json, routing-trace.ndjson.gz (metadata only), retention-snapshot.json, kms-signature.txt
manifest.json includes commitment_id, tenant_id, time_range, lexicon_hash, and file-level SHA256 hashes
Signed manifest is produced using HSM-backed KMS key and timestamped by our audit service
